g9-economics-ue2-t1.overview: The Basic Economic Problems: Scarcity, Choice, and Opportunity Cost sits inside The Basic Economic Problems and Economic Systems. Economic systems and the problem of scarcity are the focus of Unit 2 of Grade 9 Economics in the Ethiopian (FDRE Ministry of Education) curriculum. First, it explains scarcity, choice, and opportunity cost, and draws the production possibilities frontier. Then it sets out the three central questions that every economy must answer. Finally, it compares the four economic systems: traditional, capitalist, command, and mixed. Students will also learn how economic systems shape real-life production and distribution choices.
objectives: Define scarcity, choice, and opportunity cost.
Calculate the opportunity cost of a good from a production possibilities schedule.
Explain the three central questions of every economy.
Compare traditional, capitalist, command, and mixed economies.
Describe how economic growth shifts the PPF outward.
g9-economics-ue2-t1.simple:
The Basic Economic Problems: Scarcity, Choice, and Opportunity Cost in plain words. The exam wants you to recognise the core ideas, not to memorise whole paragraphs. Focus on:
  • First, scarcity as the imbalance between unlimited wants and limited resources.
  • Distinguishing scarcity from a shortage.
  • Then choice and opportunity cost, the value of the next best alternative given up.
  • Also the production possibilities frontier (PPF) and the law of increasing opportunity cost.
g9-economics-ue2-t1.detailed:
The Basic Economic Problems: Scarcity, Choice, and Opportunity Cost — the essentials. First, scarcity as the imbalance between unlimited wants and limited resources. Distinguishing scarcity from a shortage. Then choice and opportunity cost, the value of the next best alternative given up. Also the production possibilities frontier (PPF) and the law of increasing opportunity cost. Finally, economic growth as an outward shift of the PPF.

What the MoE expects you to be able to do:

  • Define scarcity, choice, and opportunity cost.
  • Calculate the opportunity cost of a good from a production possibilities schedule.
  • Explain the three central questions of every economy.
  • Compare traditional, capitalist, command, and mixed economies.
  • Describe how economic growth shifts the PPF outward.

keyTerms.def: First, scarcity as the imbalance between unlimited wants and limited resources.
Then choice and opportunity cost, the value of the next best alternative given up.
Finally, economic growth as an outward shift of the PPF.

g9-economics-ue2-t3.simple:
Economic Systems in plain words. The exam wants you to recognise the core ideas, not to memorise whole paragraphs. Focus on:
  • First, the traditional economy, which relies on custom, barter, and subsistence.
  • Then the capitalist or free-market economy, resting on private property and consumer sovereignty.
  • Also the command or socialist economy, with collective ownership and central planning.
  • Finally, the mixed economy, where public and private sectors coexist.
